name: question
label: Creatine and cognition
subject: Does creatine supplementation improve cognitive performance in healthy adults?

stages.label: Found 35 papers → 29 unique (via crossref, europepmc, openalex)

result.question: Does creatine supplementation improve cognitive performance in healthy adults?
result.headline: Creatine modestly enhances cognitive performance in healthy adults, especially during sleep deprivation.
result.answer: Creatine supplementation has been shown to improve cognitive performance in healthy adults, particularly under conditions of sleep deprivation, with benefits observed on tasks such as the DCT, logical and numerical tests, and the Psychomotor Vigilance Test [5][7][8][9][10]. The effect appears dose‑dependent, with higher doses yielding larger gains, and was demonstrated in short‑term studies involving physically active men and mixed‑sex healthy adults.

caveats.text: Effects were demonstrated in physically active men and healthy adults, so results may not extend to older, sedentary, or clinical populations.
Benefits were dose‑dependent, with higher doses (0.35 g/kg) showing larger improvements than lower doses (0.2 g/kg).
Most cognitive benefits were observed during sleep deprivation, so effects under normal rested conditions are less certain.
Studies used short‑term protocols (single dose or 7‑day loading), leaving long‑term effects unknown.
Different cognitive tests were used (DCT, logical/numerical tasks, PVT), so the magnitude of benefit may vary by task.

whatWouldSettleIt: A large, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial assessing multiple cognitive domains in a diverse adult sample over several weeks of creatine supplementation under normal sleep conditions.

evidence.text: CrM improved sleep quality compared to PL, as measured with the SSQ scale.
evidence.source: Effects of Creatine Monohydrate Loading on Sleep Metrics, Physical Performance, Cognitive Function, and Recovery in Physically Active Men: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial.

evidence.text: CrM was associated with an earlier in-bed time.
evidence.source: Effects of Creatine Monohydrate Loading on Sleep Metrics, Physical Performance, Cognitive Function, and Recovery in Physically Active Men: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial.

evidence.text: CrM did not affect sleep latency, sleep efficiency, or total sleep time.
evidence.outcome: sleep latency, sleep efficiency, total sleep time
evidence.source: Effects of Creatine Monohydrate Loading on Sleep Metrics, Physical Performance, Cognitive Function, and Recovery in Physically Active Men: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial.

evidence.text: CrM resulted in significantly lower muscle soreness scores, as measured by the Hooper questionnaire.
evidence.source: Effects of Creatine Monohydrate Loading on Sleep Metrics, Physical Performance, Cognitive Function, and Recovery in Physically Active Men: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial.

evidence.text: CrM improved cognitive performance on the DCT.
evidence.source: Effects of Creatine Monohydrate Loading on Sleep Metrics, Physical Performance, Cognitive Function, and Recovery in Physically Active Men: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial.

evidence.text: CrM enhanced TD and BD during the 5mSRT.
evidence.source: Effects of Creatine Monohydrate Loading on Sleep Metrics, Physical Performance, Cognitive Function, and Recovery in Physically Active Men: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial.

evidence.text: A single dose of 0.2 g/kg creatine is associated with a reduced deterioration in cognitive performance during sleep deprivation.
evidence.source: Single-Dose Creatine Reduces Sleep Deprivation-Induced Deterioration in Cognitive Performance.

evidence.text: Creatine mitigates sleep deprivation-induced deterioration in logical and numerical tasks, language-related processing speed, and the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT).
evidence.source: Single-Dose Creatine Reduces Sleep Deprivation-Induced Deterioration in Cognitive Performance.

evidence.text: Females benefit more than males in logic, PVT, and processing speed in language and logic tasks.
evidence.source: Single-Dose Creatine Reduces Sleep Deprivation-Induced Deterioration in Cognitive Performance.

evidence.text: The effect is less pronounced than with a high dose of 0.35 g/kg, with an improvement of up to 12%.
evidence.source: Single-Dose Creatine Reduces Sleep Deprivation-Induced Deterioration in Cognitive Performance.
